description:
FILED s470bs (Opus) while shipping #1031/#1033/#1047/#1048/#1049.
PRE-EXISTING, both emission paths.  It is the OTHER half of #1044's question:
#1044 is "the paren-argument path never asks the bareword classifier"; this is
"the OPERAND path asks and gets the wrong answer for an undeclared name".

REPRO (scratch/s470bs/p02-nope.pl):

    open(FH,"<","/etc/passwd");
    print((-e NOPE) ? 1 : 0), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  0     (with "-e on unopened filehandle NOPE"), $! = EBADF
  PCL:          dies  "Undefined subroutine &main::NOPE called"

EMISSION:  (p--e (p-scalar-ctx (pl-NOPE)))     <-- a CALL
     vs    (p--e FH)                           <-- correct, because `open(FHâ¦)`
                                                   earlier in the FILE told the
                                                   compiler FH is a handle

So the discriminator today is "is this bareword known to be a filehandle IN
THIS FILE", not perl's rule.  perl's rule for an EXPR slot (`stat lstat -X`)
is: a DECLARED sub is CALLED, and otherwise the bareword is a HANDLE NAME
(probed 5.40.3 with the warning text as discriminator â see #1044's addendum,
which established the three-rule model).  `%p-fh-arg` already quotes a bare
symbol correctly at the runtime end; the compiler just has to stop turning an
undeclared bareword into a call.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: `t/op/stat_errors.t` is written as
`my $res = eval "$op $arg"` over 29 ops x 11 args, and its arguments are
BAREWORDS (NEVEROPENED, SCALARFILE, CLOSEDFILE, CLOSEDDIR, _).  Inside a
string eval there is no `open` to teach the compiler, so EVERY one of those
becomes `(pl-NEVEROPENED)` and dies inside the eval.  `is $res, undef` passes
by accident (the eval yields undef), but `is 0+$err, EBADF` cannot: the die
never touched `$!`.  That is the file's 311 `error from -X HANDLE` rows.
s470bs fixed the runtime side of #1033 completely â every one of those errnos
is now correct when the operand actually REACHES the runtime â and the file
still reads 305/333 because of this.

MEASURED, on the s470bs tree (scratch/s470bs/p04c.pl, the `eval "$op $spell"`
matrix):  every `eval "-X FH"` / `eval "stat FH"` row dies; the same ops on
`*FH`, `\*FH` and `$lex` are all correct.  So the bug is exactly "a bareword,
in a fragment with no open".

FIX SHAPE (untried, and it is #1044's ONE predicate): ask the bareword
classifier the perl question â is a sub of this name DECLARED â rather than
"is this a known handle in this file".  #1044's CAUTION applies unchanged:
`sub SPATH {â¦} -e SPATH` must keep emitting `(p--e (pl-SPATH))`, and guard rows
21-23 of Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t assert it.  If the fix widens a classifier,
the s372 gate-SET scan over both populations is the bar.

=== DONE (s470bx, 2026-09-06) ===

FIXED, and #1044 with it â they really are ONE predicate seen from two sides,
as the brief said.  perl's rule for an EXPR handle slot (`stat`, `lstat`, the
26 filetests) is: a DECLARED sub is CALLED, anything else is a FILEHANDLE
NAME.  PCL asked a different question â "is this bareword a handle REGISTERED
IN THIS FILE" â which is why `-e NOPE` compiled to a CALL and died unless some
other statement in the same file happened to put NOPE in a handle slot.

TWO FACES, ONE PREDICATE `_expr_slot_keeps_call`:
  * `Pl/Environment.pm` marks `stat` and `lstat` `expr_slot => 1` in the
    builtin `*`-prototype table â the FACT lives in the table, consumed
    generically.  `_read_star_slot_bareword`'s builtin half now leaves the
    CALL for a callable name there, which is #1044: `sub SPATH {â¦} stat SPATH`
    is 13 elements in perl and was 0/EBADF here.  The GLOB slots (open, tell,
    eof, fileno, close, binmode, seek) keep the opposite rule, unchanged.
  * `Pl/PExpr.pm`'s `_expr_slot_bareword_operand` answers the same question
    for a FILETEST, which is an OPERATOR and has no prototype record.  The two
    share `_bareword_slot_word` (the plain-Word / one-child-funcall unwrap,
    extracted from `_read_star_slot_bareword` â it was already written there)
    and `_expr_slot_keeps_call`.

THE STRING-EVAL HORIZON was the hard half, and it is where the first attempt
broke `eval "-e SPATH"`.  The fragment is transpiled without the enclosing
program's sub table, so the compiler CANNOT answer and must not guess: it now
DEFERS in eval mode, and `%p-fh-arg` gains a third mode `:expr-slot` whose
`(pl-NAME)` arm fires only when NAME is not `fboundp` â the macro expands
INSIDE the eval, in the image where `pl-SPATH` either exists or does not,
which is the closest PCL gets to perl's own compile-time question.  ALL-CAPS
is required there too, so a genuinely mistyped sub keeps failing LOUDLY as an
undefined function rather than silently as EBADF.

ACCEPTED RESIDUE: a LOWER-CASE bareword in one of these slots stays a CALL,
although perl reads it as a handle name too (probed: `-e nope` is EBADF even
under `use strict`).  #266's asymmetry is the reason â PCL's compile-time name
knowledge is incomplete and an absence of knowledge must fail loudly.  The
gate is `Pl::Environment::fh_bareword_shape`, the same one every sibling site
uses.

ROWS: t/op/stat_errors.t 532/106 -> 636/2, i.e. 104 rows fixed, 0 new.  The
two that remain are `error from -T \*_` and `error from -B \*_`, a different
question (the -T/-B glob-ref-to-`_` operand).  t/op/filetest.t unchanged at
369/65.

BARS: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; emission-ab over 1035 files shows the
same five files as #1043 and nothing else (RCDIFF 0), so this change alters no
emission in any corpus; **gate-SET scan over BOTH populations (638 files
each), vs a fcf076f1 extraction: IDENTICAL** â mandatory here because the fix
WIDENS what the classifier accepts.

GUARD: `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t` rows 86-98 (x2 emission paths).  EACH of
ZZFTONLY / ZZSTONLY / ZZMONLY / ZZEVAL is used ONCE in ONE slot on purpose: a
first draft reused one name for three rows and FOUR of them went green against
the broken tree, because the old discriminator was file-wide.  Rows 21-23 (a
declared sub / a constant in a READ slot is CALLED) stay green, as #1044's own
caution required.  Inverse-verified: 42 of the 54 new rows fail on the
fcf076f1 extraction, and the program ABORTS there at row 86 â which is the
bug's real cost.

`docs/ir-spec.md` Â§10c carries the rule (the bareword paragraph and the
glob-slot contrast), per the "extend it, do not fork it" instruction.
subject: BLOCKER for t/op/stat_errors.t's 311 errno rows: an UNDECLARED, UNOPENED bareword in a filetest / stat OPERAND slot is emitted as a CALL `(pl-NAME)` and DIES ("Undefined subroutine &main::NOPE called") where perl answers undef with EBADF.
